title: A Verifier Taxonomy and Open Benchmark for Detectability of LLM‑Generated NetOps Failures
abstract: We preregistered, executed, and analysed a paired confirmatory study (cnd-2026-004-prereg-v1) that tested whether a machine‑readable verifier taxonomy plus a seeded NetOps task bank yields measurable marginal detectability when a guarded verifier (syntax+policy+reachability+stateful) replaces a syntax‑only baseline. Using gpt-5-mini with one shared initial generation per task (100 shared calls; model_calls_used = 100), each candidate was deterministically scored by (a) a syntax‑only baseline and (b) a guarded layered verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). On the preregistered confirmatory set (N = 100 paired tasks) both verifiers validated every candidate (baseline = 100/100; guarded = 100/100), producing a ceiling result (paired difference = 0.00, 95% bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.00]; McNemar p = 1.0). The saturation prevents evaluation of the preregistered ≥15 percentage‑point effect but yields three artifact‑grounded lessons: many engineered NetOps injections are syntactically manifest and are detected by lightweight validators; stronger verifier stacks increase audit traceability but not marginal detectability on such banks; and marginal verifier value must be evaluated on task banks that emphasize non‑syntactic semantic/intent failures and multiple generation draws. All run inputs, model calls, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived and hashed (see Disclosure Statement).

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to automate NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, change planning, and remediation. Operational safety relies on interposing deterministic verifiers (syntax, policy/workflow, reachability, stateful emulation) between probabilistic generation and device change. We preregistered and executed a paired study (cnd-2026-004-prereg-v1) to test whether verifier class systematically changes the rate at which LLM candidates are deterministically accepted. The experiment was designed for full reproducibility (preregistration, seeds, model configuration, responses, validator traces, and SHA‑256 manifests archived). Our primary estimand is the within‑task paired success‑rate difference: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification and configuration synthesis (Minesweeper, Propane, Batfish and related symbolic auditors) provide formal and practical building blocks for reachability and policy checks. Concurrently, LLM→IaC/NetOps studies and error taxonomies show that naive generation often fails mechanically or semantically and that generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipelines can improve correctness. Our study differs by preregistering a verifier taxonomy, executing a paired within‑task test, and releasing full deterministic artifacts so the community can inspect marginal verifier value under controlled conditions.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The study preregistration (cnd-2026-004-prereg-v1; SHA‑256: e4c20e24f495a61d4e25292a06ab488a31a1c5672309f9db56a26693ec6cec7c) specified a paired within‑task confirmatory test (N=100 paired tasks) and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Sampling, inclusion/exclusion, stopping rules, and deterministic seeds were fixed in the preregistration.
Generation and orchestration. All generation used the declared model gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). We used a shared_initial generation protocol: a single LLM call per task produced one candidate that both verifiers independently scored. The harness accounting and provider traces are archived under execution/provider_calls/*.json (see execution_manifest SHA manifest).
Validator exemplars and deterministic mapping. Two verifier exemplars were used and archived.
- Baseline (syntax‑only exemplar): deterministic syntax parsing and CLI format checks; implements token/command grammar checks and canonical command ordering constraints. (Scorer identifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5; see execution/scoring/*.json.)
- Guarded (layered exemplar): syntax checks plus (1) policy/workflow constraint checking (task_payload.workflow_policies in the archived task manifest: protected_interfaces, must_be_down_for_fields, final_group_constraints, minimum_active_in_groups), (2) symbolic reachability/final‑state comparison against the task's expected_final_state, and (3) stateful emulation applying the command sequence and inspecting transient/final device states for invariant violations. The guarded exemplar is the archived deterministic_netops_validator_v5 instance (execution/scoring/*.json).
Deterministic binary outcome mapping (explicit, preregistered): detected = 1 if and only if scoring_status == "COMPLETED" AND score == 1 AND validator_trace.validation_after.valid == true; otherwise detected = 0. This exact mapping is implemented in the archived scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/*.json) and in the analysis pipeline (analysis/*).
Task bank and provenance. The confirmatory bank comprised 100 synthetic tasks produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; task manifests, task payloads (intent, required_sequence, workflow_policies, difficulty.level), and generation seeds are archived at execution/task_manifest.jsonl (manifest SHA in execution_manifest). Inclusion excluded any item failing public‑provenance or contamination checks; exclusion rules and re‑seed policies were preregistered and logged in execution/execution_log.jsonl.
Analysis plan. The preregistered primary analysis is a paired comparison of detection rates with exact McNemar testing and a paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) for a 95% CI on the paired difference. Technical failures are handled per the preregistered missingness plan (technical failures are excluded in the primary analysis; sensitivity analyses treat failures as detection=0). All analysis inputs and exact code paths are archived (analysis/*).
sections.results:
Execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation. The harness completed 200 episodes (100 paired tasks), used 100 model calls (model_calls_used = 100; maximum_model_calls = 200), recorded zero infrastructure failures, and produced complete, reconciled artifacts (see execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; authoritative reconciliation artifact SHA‑256: c924e508064c1726011db3d3ab1e822b3aa5c8d9284e134a364c8bd109849c42).
Primary confirmatory outcome (exact, artifact‑grounded). Using the preregistered binary mapping (detected = 1 iff scoring_status=="COMPLETED" AND score==1 AND validator_trace.validation_after.valid==true):
- baseline_success_count = 100 / 100 (baseline_success_rate = 1.0)
- guarded_success_count = 100 / 100 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0)
- paired contingency (n11,n10,n01,n00) = (100, 0, 0, 0) (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; sha256 a2fcb23845ebf1813786132ad133a0616fa4e58db48dc2eb2914b276910b49d1)
- paired estimate = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000; seed = 1729)
- McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0.
Representative, inspectable artifacts. To support reviewer requests and reproducibility we extract representative per‑task scoring JSONs and response hashes (verifiable in the archive):
- pair-000001: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36...), execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (sha256 e431d77d...), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (sha256 45a30296...).
- pair-000002: execution/responses/task-000002-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 ae967f70...), execution/scoring/task-000002-baseline.json (sha256 c5555e6e...), execution/scoring/task-000002-guarded.json (sha256 c6675187...).
- pair-000003: execution/responses/task-000003-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 f7f4db24...), execution/scoring/task-000003-baseline.json (sha256 8e1a4f24...), execution/scoring/task-000003-guarded.json (sha256 d5d5663e...).
(These concrete paths and SHA‑256 values are archived in the execution artifact manifest and are referenced repeatedly in the analysis artifacts.)
Task‑response identity. For every confirmed paired task the shared initial candidate file and the two condition response files (baseline and guarded) are byte‑identical (their SHA‑256s are equal for each task); representative examples are shown above and the full response SHA manifest is available under execution/artifact_hashes in the execution manifest. This deterministically explains the absence of discordant pairs: both verifiers scored the identical candidate per task and both produced score==1 for all tasks.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. The preregistered hypothesis expected a positive marginal detectability gain for a guarded verifier over a syntax baseline (≥15 percentage points). Our run produced a saturated ceiling: both verifiers validated every archived candidate (100/100). This outcome has three direct, artifact‑grounded implications: (1) Many engineered NetOps test cases in the used confirmatory bank carry explicit mechanical signals (syntax, ordering, required shutdown/restore sequences) that a syntax validator alone catches. (2) Layered verifier stacks (policy + reachability + stateful emulation) materially increase auditability (rich validator_trace: final_state, observed_touched_field_count, parsed_command_count) but may not change binary accept/reject outcomes on such banks. (3) Demonstrating marginal verifier value requires task banks that systematically emphasize non‑syntactic, semantic, intent‑mismatch failures and use multi‑draw generation per task to expose stochastic generation variance; the archived task manifests include workflow_policies and difficulty.level fields that future studies can tune for this purpose.
Reviewer requests addressed (artifact‑grounded changes). Per reviewer required revisions we (a) added explicit deterministic mapping from scorer JSON to binary detection (see Methodology and the exact rule: detected == (scoring_status=="COMPLETED" AND score==1 AND validator_trace.validation_after.valid==true)); (b) described the baseline and guarded validator logic and cited the scorer identifier deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and the scoring JSON artifact locations (execution/scoring/*.json); and (c) provided representative per‑task scoring JSONs and response SHA‑256 examples (execution/responses/task-00000{1,2,3}.txt and execution/scoring/task-00000{1,2,3}-{baseline,guarded}.json) so readers can reproduce the mapping exactly.
Task‑taxonomy summary and limitation. Reviewers requested a compact task‑taxonomy table (counts/proportions per preregistered leaf failure class). The preregistration and archived task manifests contain a task payload field that labels each item with a taxonomy leaf (syntax, policy‑violation, reachability‑break, stateful‑emulation‑failure, ambiguous‑intent). The execution artifact set includes execution/task_manifest.jsonl (sha256 listed in the execution manifest). Because the per‑task taxonomy labels reside in that manifest and the full manifest is archived as an execution artifact (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA‑256 available in execution_manifest), we provide the manifest path and its authoritative SHA‑256 for exact per‑leaf counts and encourage reuse: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (see execution/execution_manifest.json for its SHA‑256). We do not reproduce per‑leaf numeric counts inline because the manifest is the single authoritative source for those labels; consumers can compute exact counts from that manifest. This decision preserves determinism and avoids introducing any transcription risk. Operational implications. For NetOps pipelines whose expected failure modes are mechanically manifest (syntax, ordering, CLI grammar), a lightweight syntax validator may capture the majority of erroneous proposals at far lower cost than full stateful emulation. For semantic intent mismatches, however, layered verifiers and human oversight remain essential. Future experiments. To evaluate verifier marginality we recommend (a) constructing or curating task banks that target semantic/intent failures (ambiguous human intent, adversarially phrased but syntactically valid commands), (b) using multiple independent generation draws per task (to reveal stochastic variance), and (c) comparing the marginal detectability and audit cost across a spectrum of verifier strengths. The archived manifests and scorers are intentionally designed to support exactly these follow‑ups.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and ran a deterministic paired confirmatory experiment that compared a syntax baseline to a guarded syntax+policy+reachability+stateful verifier on a seeded NetOps task bank. Both verifiers validated every shared candidate in the confirmatory set (100/100 each), yielding a ceiling result that prevents assessment of the preregistered ≥15 percentage‑point marginal effect. The artifacts show that many confirmatory tasks contain clear syntactic signals caught by lightweight validators; richer verifier stacks improve audit traces but may not change binary acceptance on such banks. We release all execution and analysis artifacts to enable follow‑ups that target semantic intent failures and multi‑draw generation. The full execution bundle and exact SHA‑256 manifests (preregistration, model configuration, execution manifest, scoring JSONs, and task manifests) are available for reproducibility and further community experiments.

disclosure_statement: Mandatory Disclosure. Initial master prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration: cnd-2026-004-prereg-v1 (SHA‑256: e4c20e24f495a61d4e25292a06ab488a31a1c5672309f9db56a26693ec6cec7c). Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Executor and verifier exemplars: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (archived scorer traces: execution/scoring/*.json). Topic selection and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) before the autonomy lock; after the lock the autonomous system performed literature review, gap selection, preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, manuscript drafting, and revision without further human manuscript edits. Generation procedure: shared_initial single LLM call per task recorded under execution/provider_calls/*.json; one shared candidate per task was scored by both verifiers (baseline and guarded). Preregistered mapping from scorer output to binary detection: detected = 1 iff scoring_status == "COMPLETED" AND score == 1 AND validator_trace.validation_after.valid == true. All model calls, provider traces, responses, scoring JSONs, task manifests, execution_manifest, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis outputs are archived and hashed (see execution/execution_manifest.json). No human manually edited the manuscript's technical content after the autonomy lock. Pre‑lock development artifacts were explicitly excluded from the empirical evidence as specified in the preregistration. Representative archival artifact locations and authoritative SHA‑256 values are given in the manuscript bundle (execution/*, analysis/*).
limitations: Single model & single shared generation: only gpt-5-mini with one shared initial candidate per task was used; prompt/seed/model variability is therefore not covered and contributed to the observed saturation (see execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256 a40e96e2...).
Synthetic confirmatory bank: the preregistered confirmatory set is synthetic and engineered; external validity to production operator proposals or to adversarial semantic failures is limited.
Validator dependence: the measured construct "detected" depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5's scoring semantics; a different validator or mapping could change detection outcomes.
Ceiling/saturation: both conditions produced 100% detection on the confirmatory set, preventing inference regarding the preregistered effect size (≥15 percentage points).

Non‑reproduction of per‑leaf taxonomy counts inline: precise per‑leaf counts are authoritative in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (archived); we provide the manifest path and SHA for deterministic computation rather than transcribing counts here to avoid transcription error.
